issues.reason: Existential/definite doctrine states "Reserve the bare class symbol for a non-specific / generic object ..., never for a specific definite individual", so the definite anaphor "The mist-light" must fill (Agent sk_attract_1 ...) with a typed witness, not with mist_light, the symbol the parse simultaneously puts in the class slot of (Inheritance mist_light light).

"A bare plural in an episodic clause is a specific set, not a generic" — this clause is exactly a specific dated, located occurrence, so (Patient sk_form_1 mire_essence) asserts of the substance kind what the text says of one portion that formed in that cauldron by evening.

"the mire-essence" is a definite anaphor to the portion just formed, and the same bare-class-symbol bar plus "an anaphoric definite re-mentioning an already-minted witness reuses that witness" forbid filling Theme with the kind symbol that also fills the lantern's generic fuel object.

The bare-kind half stands for the same reason as index 2, but the dropped-modifier half is overstated: "stored" here restrictively re-identifies a referent whose storing is already asserted at top level (e13), and Coreference & anaphora resolves such a definite by symbol reuse without re-emitting the antecedent's atoms — exactly as "the two sky-cats" correctly re-emits no Cardinality.

Depositing threads on a lantern neither creates, destroys, consumes nor physically changes them, so the Thematic-roles yes/no test — and its explicit "when the test is unclear, default to Theme" — gives Theme; the same mis-slotting also rides inside e9_rule's (Patient (sk_leave $x) (sk_thread $x)).

An entity-attached "at" is licensed as LocatedIn ("LocatedIn is containment ONLY — in / at / inside / within") and the atom is true of the crowd, while Multiple live readings makes one reading the default and fires only on genuine equipoise — which the very next sentence's repeated NP epithet "The nightmoth crowd at the Harbor Row" breaks in favour of the NP attachment.

gaps_confirmed: A day-of-year number inside a bare ordinal year ("day 380 of Year 2") — the Time terms (Day n)/(Year n) are specified for a Gregorian day-of-month and calendar year, and nothing states how a fictional-calendar date of this shape renders.

An ordinal-modified noun with no associated ordering event and no stated "-est" dimension ("the second cauldron") — Ordinal's scale slot is defined only as the associated event or an explicit dimension, so the parse's (Ordinal sk_cauldron_1 2 cauldron) fills it with the comparison class, for which no licence exists.
new_gaps: No stated trigger for a bare MASS NP in an episodic clause: the "bare plural in an episodic clause is a specific set" rule is count-only (a GroupOf witness), and nothing says when a mass NP ("produced mist-light", "Mire-essence formed") mints a portion witness (Member sk_<mass>_1 <mass>) versus staying the bare kind filler that is licensed for non-specific objects ("burned mire-essence").

No licensed way to keep successive portions of one substance apart across a passage — the fuel the lantern burned, the portion that formed in the cauldron, and the portion stored and then drawn: the only mass-witness machinery lives in Partitives (a whole plus a PartOf portion of a presupposed whole), and nothing covers a portion brought newly into existence by an event or its relation to the kind symbol.
defect_summary: Index 0: mint (Member sk_mist_light_1 mist_light) at "produced mist-light" and fill (Agent sk_attract_1 sk_mist_light_1), leaving mist_light in the class slot only. Index 1: mint (Member sk_mire_essence_1 mire_essence) and emit (Patient sk_form_1 sk_mire_essence_1). Index 2: reuse that witness — (Theme sk_store_1 sk_mire_essence_1) — keeping it distinct from the kind symbol the lantern's generic fuel object legitimately fills. Index 3 (confirmed half): (Theme sk_draw_1 sk_mire_essence_1) for "the stored mire-essence". Index 4: (Theme sk_leave_1 sk_threads_1) in place of Patient, with (Theme (sk_leave $x) (sk_thread $x)) inside e9_rule.
notes: Compound decomposition, the group/cardinality handling, the per-member distribution rules, the connective-free narrative sequencing and the tense/time atoms are otherwise clean, and every head used is licensed. The Ordinal scale filler is filed above as a confirmed gap rather than an issue, per the reviewer's own routing.
